title: 'Miracle on the Mississippi': Probe Begins After Tanker Collides With Docked New Orleans Cruise Ship
snippet: Federal investigators are searching for answers after a cargo tanker lost control and rammed a docked riverboat cruise in New Orleans, sending nearly 200 people into the Mississippi River in a harrowing ordeal.
content:
Federal investigators are working to determine how a massive cargo tanker lost steering control before colliding with a docked paddlewheel cruise ship in New Orleans on Friday, causing the vessel to capsize and plunging dozens of passengers into the Mississippi River.

Despite the chaotic scene, officials confirmed that all 197 passengers aboard the American Heritage were brought to safety in what Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry called a "literal miracle on the Mississippi." While 32 people were initially hospitalized for injuries, authorities confirmed that there were no fatalities.

A Dramatic and Heroic Rescue

The collision occurred when the Atlantic Asphalt, a tanker ship built in 2017, drifted off course and struck the docked riverboat. Bystander video captured screeching metal and panicked screams as the paddlewheeler tipped onto its side and took on water. Dozens of passengers were forced to scramble over railings or leap into the river.

A rapid response from first responders, harbor police, and nearby commercial vessel crews prevented tragedy. Captain Brian Clesi of the local riverboat Creole Queen launched a rescue skiff with a crewmate, pulling nine struggle-weary passengers—many of them elderly and without life vests—out of the water.

"Everybody in this harbor works together as a team," Clesi said. "The ones that didn't have a life jacket on were holding on for dear life."

Lawsuits and Salvage Operations

Hours after the wreck, the Port of New Orleans filed a federal lawsuit seeking the seizure of the Atlantic Asphalt. The filing cites gross negligence by the tanker's Liberia-based ownership group and Singapore-based manager, alleging more than $1 million in damage to the port terminal.

U.S. Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham confirmed the tanker was under the command of a local river pilot when it apparently lost steering capability. Officials emphasized there is no indication of terrorism. A team from the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has arrived on scene to lead the formal investigation.

Engineers now face the complex task of recovering the capsized American Heritage. Before salvage crews can lift the riverboat, they must siphon approximately 16,000 gallons of fuel from its tanks to prevent an environmental spill in the busy commercial waterway.
